content.title: Nuggets vs. Lakers: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/14/26)
content.text: The Denver Nuggets (41–26) visit the Los Angeles Lakers (41–25) today at Crypto.com Arena in L.A. in a primetime Western Conference powerhouse matchup. Denver comes in off two big wins amid one of the toughest stretches of its season. After falling to the New York Knicks and Oklahoma City Thunder, the Nuggets responded with a 129–93 rout of the Houston Rockets on Wednesday and a 136–131 win in a shootout with the San Antonio Spurs. With Victor Wembanyama sidelined for San Antonio, Denver still faced a major challenge, trailing by 16 at halftime and by as many as 20 points. The Nuggets erupted for 83 second-half points, powered by the Jamal Murray–Nikola Jokic tandem, which combined for 70 points. Jokic capped the performance with yet another triple-double. Denver currently sits sixth in the Western Conference, just a half-game behind the Lakers. A win tonight would push the Nuggets as high as third place in the tightly packed standings. Los Angeles, meanwhile, has surged with four straight victories, including a 142–130 shootout win over the Chicago Bulls on Thursday. Luka Doncic led the way with 51 points — his highest scoring performance since joining the Lakers. Austin Reaves continued his strong recent form with 30 points, while LeBron James returned to the lineup with an all-around effort of 18 points, seven rebounds, and seven assists. Reaves is averaging 28.7 points over his last three games. Expect a Wild Western Conference shootout that’ll go down to the wire. Denver has the edge here with greater depth on both ends. Prediction: Denver Nuggets 129, Los Angeles Lakers 127 Injury Report Denver Nuggets KJ Simpson — Out (Ankle) Jamal Murray — GTD (Ankle) Aaron Gordon — GTD (Hamstring) Peyton Watson — Out (Hamstring) Los Angeles Lakers Maxi Kleber — Out (Back) How to Watch Nuggets vs. Lakers Tip-off for today’s Nuggets-Lakers game is set for 8:30 PM Eastern / 6:30 PM Mountain / 5:30 PM Pacific at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. The game airs live on ABC and streams on the ABC and ESPN apps and websites. You can watch the game for free on your local ABC affiliate with an antenna, or at no additional cost through most existing cable, satellite, or live-TV streaming packages. If you’re a cord-cutter without an active livestreaming plan, you can watch the game for free by taking advantage of free trials from DIRECTV Stream, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo TV, or YouTube TV. Hulu + Live TV includes Disney+ and ESPN Unlimited as part of its standard plan.
